Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Ashok Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.M. Yadav, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.344 of 2022, registered under Sections 420, 406, 120B and 417 IPC at Police Station- Dhampur,
District Bijnor with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

4. As per prosecution story, Rs.1 lakh each is stated to have been deposited in the company by several persons at the behest of the named accused persons on the pretext that the same shall be Mohak Dixit vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39574757/
1 doubled within a stipulated period of time.

entities.text: Mohak Dixit vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Neither the deposited money was returned nor the profit was given.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He is not named in the FIR.
His name has come up later on during investigation in the statement of co-accused person, which is not admissible in evidence.
Learned counsel has further stated that the applicant has been nominated in five cases of similar nature and he is not named in either of them.
The applicant has been enlarged on anticipatory bail in two of the cases.
The applicant has no previous criminal history except the said cases foisted against him.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that the matter has been settled between the parties.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel for the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.
7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

8. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.
9. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iv). that in case charge-sheet is submitted the applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during the trial;
(v). that the applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness;

(vi). that the applicant shall appear before the trial court on each date fixed unless personal presence is exempted;
(vii). that in case of breach of any of the above conditions the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail.
10. It is made clear that observations made hereinabove are exclusively for deciding the instant anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial.
